tasks.short: Build the monthly HR and flex reports for the HR Director, site managers and the works council from AFAS and Power BI.

today.trigger: Calendar: month close, MT meeting, quarterly OR meeting, or an ad-hoc request from a manager or the HR Director.
steps: Check that the nightly AFAS extract in Power BI refreshed and the numbers match AFAS
Export headcount, verzuim, hires and flex hours to Excel per site
Merge agency portal hours and Recruitee pipeline data by hand
Write commentary on what moved and why
Paste charts into PowerPoint or Word and mail them out
drudgery: Copying the same charts into slides every month
Reconciling agency hours with AFAS cost centres
Rewording the same commentary
today.time_sinks: Data checks and manual merging of agency and Recruitee data take more time than the analysis; one-off requests interrupt the planned work.

lenses.faster: Standard reports come from one Power BI model that already joins AFAS, Recruitee and agency data; an LLM drafts the commentary from the month-on-month changes, and the analyst edits it in minutes.
lenses.autonomous: After the nightly refresh passes its data checks at month close, the report pack builds itself and waits for the analyst's sign-off before it goes out.
lenses.ambitious: Every site manager gets a monthly one-page report on their own team: verzuim, 90-day retention, flex share and open roles, with the three things that need action.
lenses.joy: No more pasting screenshots into slides; the analyst spends the time on the question behind the numbers.
lenses.options: For an ad-hoc request the analyst gets three report angles (by site, by shift, by contract type) and picks the one that answers the question.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the report catalogue, the metric definitions and the commentary rules instead of producing each report.
reach: Monthly management commentary that HR Business Partners now write
Flex labour cost reporting that FP&A Analysts compile
OR information pack the HR Director assembles

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which number will trigger a difficult conversation with a site manager or the OR, and framing it so it leads to action rather than defence.
tasks.pattern_why: Data extraction and charts are deterministic Power BI work; only the written commentary is unstructured and needs an LLM inside a fixed pipeline with human sign-off.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS refresh succeeds on the first working day after month close.
steps: Power BI runs data quality checks (row counts, totals versus AFAS payroll journal)
Paginated report pack renders per audience
LLM drafts commentary from the variance table, citing the figures it used
Analyst reviews, edits and approves
Power Automate distributes to the mailing list and SharePoint
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves commentary and figures before distribution; reports for the OR are also checked by the HR Director.
data_needed: AFAS headcount, contracts, absence and payroll extract
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint report archive with version, approver and date; Power BI refresh history.

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI can generate narrative summaries of report pages.
Power BI paginated reports and subscriptions can distribute reports on a schedule.
LLM commentary drafted from a variance table saves most of the writing time while the analyst still checks it.

risks: LLM commentary states a cause that is not in the data
Small-team figures in site reports identify individuals (AVG/GDPR), especially absence data
Agency data arrives late and the pack goes out incomplete
research_questions: How many hours per month go into standard versus ad-hoc reports today?
Can the three agency portals deliver hours data in a machine-readable export on a fixed date?
Does the OR accept AI-drafted commentary if the analyst signs it, and does it want this noted?
What minimum group size must reports use to avoid identifying employees in absence figures?

tasks.short: Make sure managers, HRBPs and finance get the right dashboards and data on time, with the right access.

today.trigger: Requests for access, new managers, reorganisations, and complaints that a dashboard is stale.
steps: Grant or remove Power BI workspace and row-level security access by hand
Chase the nightly refresh when it fails
Send reminder mails that a report is updated
Answer 'where can I find' questions in Teams
drudgery: Keeping row-level security in line with AFAS org changes
Repeating where-to-find answers
Checking refresh failures each morning
today.time_sinks: Access changes after every manager change and failed refreshes found only when a user complains.

lenses.faster: Access follows the AFAS org structure automatically, so the manual grant and remove work disappears.
lenses.autonomous: A failed refresh or a stale dataset triggers an alert and a status banner on the dashboard before users notice; a manager change in AFAS updates their Power BI access overnight.
lenses.ambitious: Each manager receives a short weekly digest in Teams with only the signals for their team (expiring certificates, open roles, long-term absence milestones) instead of having to open dashboards.
lenses.joy: No morning refresh checking and no access tickets; the analyst talks to users about what they need instead.
lenses.options: Users choose the channel: Teams digest, email summary or dashboard only.
lenses.altitude: The analyst designs the distribution rules, data access policy and service levels rather than delivering information by hand.
reach: Access administration that HR Administrators do for managers
Studytube certificate expiry reminders that L&D Specialists send
Poortwachter milestone reminders HRBPs track

tasks.human_edge: Deciding who may see sensitive HR data and explaining that choice to managers and the OR.
tasks.pattern_why: Access and alerts follow written rules on structured AFAS and Power BI data; no model is needed to run it.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS refresh completes or fails; an org change in AFAS.
steps: Script reads AFAS org and manager data and syncs Entra security groups
Power BI row-level security uses those groups
Refresh monitor posts failures to an HR data Teams channel
Power Automate sends weekly manager digests from the dataset
Analyst handles exceptions flagged by the sync
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst reviews exceptions such as managers with no AFAS team, and any access to absence data beyond the own team.
data_needed: AFAS org units and manager assignments
in_practice.logs_to: Access change log in SharePoint list plus Entra audit log; Power BI refresh history.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports row-level security based on security groups and refresh failure notifications.
Power Automate can post scheduled messages to Teams from Power BI data.
AFAS Profit exposes org and employee data through GetConnectors for syncing.

risks: Sync error grants a manager access to another team's absence data (AVG/GDPR breach)
Digest fatigue: managers ignore weekly messages
Dependence on a script nobody else understands
research_questions: How many access changes and refresh failures happen per month?
Is the manager field in AFAS reliable enough to drive access?
Does the works council need to approve automated manager digests that include absence signals?

tasks.short: Keep the Power BI model, AFAS extract, DAX measures and Excel tools working when systems or definitions change.

today.trigger: AFAS updates, new CAO rules, new cost centres or sites, user requests, broken measures.
steps: Find which tables or fields changed in the AFAS extract
Edit Power Query steps and DAX measures
Test against AFAS totals
Update documentation if time allows
Publish and tell users
drudgery: Tracing broken lineage after a field rename
Writing documentation after the fact
Manual regression checks
today.time_sinks: Finding what broke and why, and testing by eye against AFAS reports.

lenses.faster: An AI coding assistant reads the model, proposes the DAX or Power Query fix and writes the test; the analyst reviews and publishes.
lenses.autonomous: Automated tests run after every refresh and compare key totals with AFAS; a failure opens a ticket with the likely cause.
lenses.ambitious: The HR data model is put under version control with tests and documentation for the first time, so it survives the analyst being on holiday.
lenses.joy: Less detective work on broken measures, more time on new questions.
lenses.options: For a definition change (e.g. how verzuim counts partial sick days) the assistant shows two or three implementations and their effect on last year's figures.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the data model's design, tests and definitions; AI does most of the code edits.
reach: Maintaining finance Power BI models the Controller relies on
Excel tools the Compensation and Benefits Specialist keeps

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a changed number is a bug or a real business change, and agreeing metric definitions with HR and Finance.
tasks.pattern_why: The analyst stays in charge of the model; AI drafts code, tests and documentation, and changes to shared definitions need human judgement.

in_practice.trigger: A test failure after refresh, a change request, or an announced AFAS update.
steps: Assistant diffs the model and AFAS extract schema
Assistant proposes a fix and a test
Analyst reviews and runs it on a copy
Analyst publishes and the change note is generated
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves every change before publish; definition changes also signed off by the HR Director or Controller.
in_practice.logs_to: Git history and a change log in SharePoint.

evidence.claim: Power BI projects (PBIP) store models as text files that can be version controlled.
Copilot in Power BI can write and explain DAX queries.
AI coding assistants can edit model definitions and tests in a repo.

risks: Subtle DAX error passes review and changes reported figures
Model files may contain personal data if sample data is committed
Over-reliance makes the analyst lose understanding of the model
research_questions: How often does the AFAS extract break, and how long does each fix take today?
Can the current model be converted to PBIP and put in Git without exposing personal data?
Which ten totals would form a reliable regression test against AFAS?

tasks.short: Answer user questions about dashboards and reports and fix their problems.

today.trigger: Teams messages and emails from managers, HRBPs, payroll and finance.
steps: Read the question and work out which report and filter they mean
Reproduce the issue
Explain the definition or fix access or data
Reply and sometimes walk them through it in a call
drudgery: Explaining the same definitions again
Questions that are really 'which filter is on'
today.time_sinks: Interruptions and back-and-forth to understand what the user saw.

lenses.faster: A help assistant answers definition and how-to questions from the metric glossary and report docs, so the analyst only gets real problems.
lenses.autonomous: Questions in the HR data Teams channel get a first answer at once, with a link to the right page; unresolved ones go to the analyst with context attached.
lenses.ambitious: Managers can ask their own questions in plain language over the data they are allowed to see, instead of waiting for a custom report.
lenses.joy: The repeat questions go; what remains are interesting problems and teaching moments.
lenses.options: The assistant offers the user two or three ways to view their question (a filter, a different page, a new visual request).
lenses.altitude: The analyst maintains the glossary and the assistant's knowledge base and reviews what it got wrong.
reach: First-line HR systems questions HR Administrators handle
Explaining finance dashboards that FP&A answers

tasks.human_edge: Spotting when a question reveals a real data error or an unmet need, and patiently teaching managers to read data.
tasks.pattern_why: The assistant searches docs and the data model, answers simple questions and escalates; changes to data or access always go to the analyst.

in_practice.trigger: A message in the HR data Teams channel or a support form.
steps: Assistant classifies the question (definition, how-to, access, data error)
Answers definition and how-to from the glossary with a link
Routes access and data errors to the analyst with screenshots and report name
Analyst resolves and the answer is added to the knowledge base
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst handles all access, data correction and anything involving individual employee data.
in_practice.logs_to: Ticket list in SharePoint with category and resolution.

evidence.claim: Copilot Studio can build Teams agents grounded in SharePoint documents.
A large share of BI support questions are repeat definition and navigation questions.

risks: Assistant gives a confident wrong definition and a manager acts on it
Users paste employee personal data into the chat
Glossary goes stale
research_questions: What share of last quarter's questions were definitions or how-to?
Is there an up-to-date metric glossary, or must it be written first?
Will managers use a Teams assistant or still message the analyst directly?

tasks.short: Track internal customers' needs: which sites, managers and agencies drive hiring, flex use and turnover.

today.trigger: Quarterly reviews, budget season, peak season planning, or a site raising concerns.
steps: Pull hires, leavers, open roles and flex hours per site and manager
Compare agencies on fill rate, cost and flex worker turnover
Spot sites or teams with rising problems
Prepare a short note for HR Director and HRBPs
drudgery: Matching agency data with AFAS cost centres
Building the same comparison tables every quarter
today.time_sinks: Agency data in three different formats.

lenses.faster: Agency hours and invoices are loaded into one standard table, so site and agency comparisons are always ready.
lenses.autonomous: Weekly checks flag a site whose 90-day retention or agency fill rate drops below threshold and post it to the HRBP.
lenses.ambitious: An agency scorecard on fill rate, cost per hour, no-shows and conversion to permanent staff, used in contract talks with all three agencies.
lenses.joy: No more format wrangling; time goes to talking with site managers about causes.
lenses.options: Scenarios for peak season: more agency staff, earlier permanent hiring, or more overtime, with cost and retention effect.
lenses.altitude: The analyst sets the thresholds and scorecard and checks the signals rather than building tables.
reach: Agency performance review that Recruiters or the HR Director run
Flex cost forecasting done by FP&A
Agency invoice checking that Bookkeepers do

tasks.human_edge: Knowing the context behind a site's numbers (a new manager, a lost client, a hot summer) before raising an alarm.
tasks.pattern_why: Once agency exports are mapped, thresholds and scorecards are rule-based on structured data; an LLM step may only be needed to parse agency PDFs.

in_practice.trigger: Weekly scheduled run after agency hour files arrive.
steps: Load and map agency exports to AFAS cost centres
Compute site and agency metrics in Power BI
Check thresholds and create alerts
Analyst reviews alerts and adds context for HRBPs
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst reviews flagged sites and agencies before anything goes to managers or agencies.
in_practice.logs_to: Alert history table in Power BI dataset.

evidence.claim: Power BI data alerts can notify on threshold breaches.
Agency portal exports can be mapped to a standard format with a small script.

risks: Agency data quality differs, making comparisons unfair
Flex worker data falls under the agency as employer; sharing limits under AVG
Alerts without context create blame between sites
research_questions: What export formats do the three agencies offer, and can contracts require a standard one?
Do HR Director and procurement want an agency scorecard for contract talks?
Which thresholds would site managers accept as meaningful?

tasks.short: Build new HR dashboards, data models and Excel tools when HR or finance asks for them.

today.trigger: A new question or project: e.g. onboarding tracking, CAO wage table changes, verzuim deep dive.
steps: Clarify the question with the requester
Find and join data from AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube
Design the model and measures
Build the dashboard and test
Hand over and explain
drudgery: Writing boilerplate Power Query for each new source
Layout fiddling
Documentation
today.time_sinks: Getting data from Recruitee and Studytube APIs and joining them to AFAS employee IDs.

lenses.faster: AI coding builds connectors, the data model and a first dashboard from a written spec in a day instead of a week.
lenses.autonomous: Not autonomous: each new tool starts with a request and ends with analyst testing.
lenses.ambitious: Build the hire-to-productive tracker that follows each hire from Recruitee offer to day 90 in AFAS and Studytube, measuring the North Star directly.
lenses.joy: The analyst spends time on the question and design, not on boilerplate.
lenses.options: Three dashboard mock-ups shown to the requester before building.
lenses.altitude: The analyst writes specs, data contracts and acceptance tests; AI produces the build.
reach: Small tools the L&D Specialists build in Excel for certificate tracking
Recruitment dashboards Recruiters request from Recruitee

tasks.human_edge: Turning a vague request into the right question and design, and deciding what data should not be combined.
tasks.pattern_why: The analyst leads design and makes privacy choices; AI drafts code, models and visuals.

in_practice.trigger: Approved request in the HR data backlog.
steps: Analyst writes a one-page spec with questions and data sources
AI assistant drafts connectors, model and measures
AI produces mock-ups; requester picks one
Analyst tests against source totals and publishes
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst signs off build and a privacy check (DPIA if needed) before release.
in_practice.logs_to: Git repository and backlog in SharePoint or Planner.

evidence.claim: Recruitee offers an API for candidates, offers and pipeline stages.
AI coding assistants can generate Power Query and data pipeline code from a spec.

risks: Joining recruitment, learning and HR data creates new profiling that needs a DPIA and possibly OR consent (WOR art. 27)
Generated code not maintainable by others
Studytube API limits
research_questions: Can candidate IDs in Recruitee be reliably matched to AFAS employee numbers?
Does Studytube's API give completion data per employee and certificate?
Does a combined hire-to-day-90 dataset need works council approval?

tasks.short: Keep HR data clean in AFAS and compile stats on hires, transfers, appraisals and verzuim.

today.trigger: Monthly close, verzuim reports, audits, CBS or sector surveys, requests from HRBPs.
steps: Run AFAS data checks for missing or wrong fields
Ask HR Administrators to correct records
Compile hires, transfers, leavers and absence rates per site
Fill in survey or audit templates
drudgery: Hunting for missing end dates and wrong cost centres
Filling external survey forms by hand

lenses.faster: Data quality rules run nightly and produce a fix list; statistics come straight from the model.
lenses.autonomous: Each night, broken records (no manager, contract ended but active, absence without notice date) are sent as tasks to the HR Administrator queue; monthly stats are produced without asking.
lenses.ambitious: Clean data good enough to trust 90-day retention per manager and recruiter channel, which nobody can measure reliably today.
lenses.joy: No more chasing corrections by email.
lenses.options: Stats can be shown under alternative definitions (e.g. verzuim with and without long-term cases) side by side.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the data quality rules and definitions; administrators fix records.
reach: Record audits HR Administrators do
Verzuim statistics for the occupational health service HRBPs prepare
Headcount reconciliation the Payroll Specialist does at close

tasks.human_edge: Deciding which errors matter and agreeing definitions with HR and payroll.
tasks.pattern_why: Quality rules and statistics are written rules on structured AFAS data.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract and month close.
steps: Run data quality rules on the extract
Create correction tasks in AFAS workflow or a SharePoint list
Compute monthly statistics in Power BI
Analyst reviews exceptions and signs off monthly figures
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst signs off monthly statistics; administrators confirm each record correction in AFAS.
data_needed: AFAS employee, contract, absence and appraisal records
in_practice.logs_to: Data quality issue log with open and closed dates.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit supports workflows and tasks for record changes.
Rule-based data quality checks on HR extracts are standard BI practice.

risks: Absence data includes health-related details; only keep what Poortwachter and AVG allow
Administrators get too many low-value tasks
Definitions differ from payroll's, causing two truths
research_questions: How many record errors per month are found today and how are they fixed?
Can AFAS workflows receive tasks created from outside?
Are verzuim definitions agreed between HR, payroll and the occupational health service?

tasks.short: Analyse labour market and regional trends around Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo that affect hiring and wages.

today.trigger: Strategy sessions, CAO negotiations, opening a new site, recruitment problems.
steps: Collect data from CBS StatLine, UWV, sector reports and agency feedback
Compare with own hiring and pay data
Write a summary with implications
Present to HR Director and MT
drudgery: Finding and downloading regional tables
Reading long sector reports
today.time_sinks: Collecting and aligning external data with own data.

lenses.faster: An assistant pulls regional CBS and UWV figures and summarises sector reports with sources, so the analyst starts from a draft.
lenses.autonomous: A quarterly brief on labour market tension, wages and vacancy numbers per region is drafted when new CBS/UWV data appears.
lenses.ambitious: A standing labour market view per site, used in workforce planning, peak season hiring and CAO preparation.
lenses.joy: No more trawling websites; time goes to interpretation.
lenses.options: Scenarios for the coming year: tight, stable, loosening labour market per region, with effect on time to hire and flex cost.
lenses.altitude: The analyst curates sources and checks the brief rather than collecting data.
reach: Market input that the Compensation and Benefits Specialist gathers
Workforce assumptions FP&A uses in budgets
Sourcing strategy input for Recruiters

tasks.human_edge: Linking external trends to Noordhaven's own situation and knowing what the MT can act on.
tasks.pattern_why: Several steps over web sources and own data with uncertain quality; the analyst checks sources and conclusions before use.

in_practice.trigger: New quarterly CBS/UWV releases or a strategy request.
steps: Agent fetches regional tables from CBS StatLine and UWV
Agent summarises recent sector reports with citations
Agent joins with own hiring and pay data
Analyst checks sources, edits implications and approves
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst checks every figure and citation before the brief goes to the MT.
in_practice.logs_to: Brief archive in SharePoint with source list.

evidence.claim: CBS StatLine provides open regional labour market data via an API.
Research agents can gather and summarise public sources with citations.

risks: Hallucinated or misattributed figures
Public data too coarse for Venlo or Tilburg area
Over-confident scenarios used in CAO talks
research_questions: Which CBS and UWV tables cover the three regions at a useful level?
How often does the MT actually use labour market input in decisions?
Would scenarios change peak season hiring timing?

role.altitude: From producing reports and fixing dashboards to owning the HR data product: metric definitions, data quality rules, access policy, tests and the AI steps that draft commentary and answer questions.
reach: Flex labour cost and agency performance reporting now done by FP&A and Recruiters
First-line HR systems and data questions handled by HR Administrators
Workforce assumptions for FP&A budgets
Market data gathering for the Compensation and Benefits Specialist
Certificate expiry tracking from Studytube for L&D
role.ceiling_note: Limited by data quality in AFAS and agency portals, API access to Recruitee and Studytube, and AVG/works council rules on combining employee data; agreeing definitions and privacy choices with people stays slow human work.
skills_to_grow: Data product ownership and metric governance
Version control and automated testing for Power BI
Privacy by design and DPIA practice under AVG and the EU AI Act
Explaining data to managers and the works council
role.ambitious_version: Build and run a hire-to-day-90 measurement system that tracks the North Star per site, manager and recruitment channel, gives every manager a weekly signal on their team, and lets HR test changes in onboarding and agency use against real retention results.
